# GEO report: acme-mugs **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 24–33/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 5.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 24. High = (5.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 33. This is read from code only. The site tells every crawler to stay out, and its pages are empty until JavaScript runs. The one unknown is the canonical address (GEO-015), because no site domain is declared. I assumed you want search and AI tools to find this site. If the block is deliberate, such as a pre-launch site, the score matters less. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking all crawlers in robots.txt - **Why it matters:** `Disallow: /` asks every search and AI-search crawler not to visit any page, so the rest of the work can't help until this is changed. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:2` - **What the code says:** `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 50–59 (GEO-009 and GEO-014 both become Clear). The cap of 40 for a site-wide block no longer applies. ### 2. Put the page text in the HTML the server sends - **Why it matters:** The server sends an empty `
`. Crawlers that don't run JavaScript see no text, and the catalogue list loads only in the browser after the page opens. - **Where:** `index.html:8` and `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:6` - **What the code says:** `
` and `fetch('/api/mugs').then((r) => r.json()).then(setItems);` - **Size:** Large. Prerender or server-render the pages, for example with a Vite SSG or SSR setup or a framework like Next.js or React Router framework mode. - **Score after this:** 37–46 on its own. Combined with item 1, 70–79. ### 3. Give the pages a real title, description and language - **Why it matters:** Every page shares the title "Vite App" and has no description or `lang`. Machines can't tell what the pages are. - **Where:** `index.html:2` and `index.html:5` - **What the code says:** `` and `Vite App` - **Size:** Small. Set `lang="en"` and add a description. Give each route its own title, for example with React 19's `` and `<meta>` elements inside the page components. - **Score after this:** 33–41 on its own. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, 2 valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers can get in | Problem | `public/robots.txt:2` blocks everyone from the whole site | | GEO-014 | Routes are indexable | Problem | `public/robots.txt:2` blocks Googlebot and Bingbot through `*`, on both routes. There is no noindex. | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on your own domain | Can't tell | No canonical is set and no site domain is declared | | GEO-003 | Main content is in the server HTML | Problem | `index.html:8`, both routes. `Catalogue.jsx:6` fetches in the browser. | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is listed in robots.txt | Problem | No sitemap file or generator, and no `Sitemap:` line | | GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Problem | `index.html:2,5`, both routes | | GEO-016 | Key pages reachable by real links | Problem | `src/main.jsx:11`, 1 of 1 routes needing a link | | GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet` found | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Problem | `Home.jsx:5` has an image with no alt. `Catalogue.jsx` is Clear, so 1 of 2 routes. | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not an app | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not present. This is not scored and not a problem. | | GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not applicable | Not an app | ## Other problems found - **Catalogue is reachable only through a click handler:** `src/main.jsx:11`: `<button onClick={() => navigate('/catalogue')}>Catalogue</button>`. Crawlers can't follow it. Use `<Link to="/catalogue">Catalogue</Link>`. This is also the cause of the GEO-016 Problem. - **Image has no alt text:** `src/pages/Home.jsx:5`: `<img src="/hero.jpg" />`. Add a short description in `alt`. ## Worth considering - **Make each mug its own page:** `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:11`: `{items.map((m) => <p key={m.id}>{m.name}</p>)}`. Each mug is only a name in a paragraph. Giving each one a page with its own address, price and description would give it something to be found and quoted for. - **Say more on the home page:** `src/pages/Home.jsx:6`: `Thrown by hand in Bristol and shipped worldwide.` Add things a buyer would ask, such as price range, shipping, returns and how to order. Right now this is the only text. Link onward to the catalogue from the page body. - **Label the business with structured data:** `src/pages/Home.jsx:4`: `Handmade ceramic mugs`. Organization or Product JSON-LD (machine-readable labels) with the name, location and mug prices might help machines understand what is sold. - **Declare the site's address:** there is no `geo.config.json` and no canonical link in `index.html`. Setting `site.origin` and a canonical tag per page would settle GEO-015. - **Add the basic head tags:** `index.html:4`: `<meta charset="utf-8" />`. There is no `viewport` or social (Open Graph) tags, so shared links and mobile rendering get no hints. - **Add a 404 route:** `src/main.jsx:20-21` defines only `/` and `/catalogue`, and there is no catch-all. A static host would likely serve the app shell with a 200 for wrong addresses. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015 (canonical):** I need your site's domain to judge this. Tell me the domain and I'll recheck. - **Real status codes and headers:** whether `/robots.txt` really answers 200, and any `X-Robots-Tag` headers set by the host, are decided outside the code. A live scan would confirm them. - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Catalogue contents:** `/api/mugs` is built at runtime, so I can't see what it returns. ## Assumptions - You want search and AI tools to find this site. If `Disallow: /` is deliberate, such as before launch, ignore items 1 and 3 above and the GEO-009 and GEO-014 results. - The two routes in `src/main.jsx` are the whole site. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
